title: Subjective examination — 10-item encounter check
_comment: applies: 'if_opportunity'    graded only if the transcript shows the situation arose;
otherwise scored not_applicable and excluded from the total
parts:   sub-criteria for compound items. All parts met = got, some = partial, none = missed.
type:    'content' = did the student ask; 'judgment' = how well did they handle it.
Judgment items are the least reliable to grade automatically — see DESIGN_NOTES.md.

items.question: Greet the patient and introduce yourself?
parts: introduced themselves by name or role

items.question: Ask if the patient is coming to you by way of direct access or from another provider?
parts: asked whether the patient was referred, self-referred, or had seen another provider

items.question: Provide an empathetic response to the patient when appropriate and validate their experience?
items.opportunity: The patient expressed pain, frustration, worry, embarrassment, or any emotional content that invited acknowledgement.
parts: responded with empathy rather than moving straight to the next question

items.question: Appropriately and empathetically redirect the patient back to the topic?
items.opportunity: The patient went off-topic, rambled, or digressed from the clinical history.
parts: brought the patient back to the clinical topic
did so without being abrupt or dismissive

items.question: Ask about the mechanism of injury or how the condition started, and if they had this problem before?
parts: asked how the injury happened or how the condition started
asked whether the patient has had this problem before

items.question: Ask about what has been done to address the pain up to this point?
parts: asked what the patient has already tried or had done for the pain

items.question: Ask about the quality of the pain (sharp, burning, numb) and the behavior of the pain (what makes it better, worse, or no different)?
parts: asked about pain quality or character
asked what makes the pain better, worse, or unchanged

items.question: Ask about how this problem is impacting function and important personal goals the patient wants to achieve?
parts: asked how the problem affects daily function or activity
asked what the patient wants to get back to doing

items.question: Ask if they have any support from friends or family if necessary?
items.opportunity: The case involves circumstances where social support is clinically relevant — for example living alone, reduced mobility, caregiving duties, complex medication management, or the patient raising a difficulty coping.
parts: asked about available support from family, friends, or others

items.question: Ask if there are any environmental factors that would result in barriers to recovery in a timely manner?
parts: asked about environmental or circumstantial barriers to recovery, such as stairs, work demands, commute, transport, or home setup

affect._comment: Read of how the patient experienced the encounter. Treat as exploratory until validated against faculty raters.

thresholds.green: Patient was largely at ease and appeared to feel heard.
thresholds.amber: Some discomfort, anxiety, or moments of not feeling understood.
thresholds.red: Patient was frequently uncomfortable, anxious, or did not feel understood.
